N002.en: >Handpan Constellation Studio · for the Neotone¹ and the Neotone Mutant<

N003.en: >Your Neotone can play anything. Now you can see it.<

N004.en: >But when you can play anything, you have no landmarks: with every scale, the notes move. The app puts seven colours on your Neotone, and those never move.<

N005.en: >€9.99 a month, first month free. We ask for your card when you sign up, and nothing is charged if you stop before the month is up.<

N011.en: >How many scales do you really play?<

N012.en: >When the notes move, don’t you get lost?<

N013.en: >I did. On a Neotone, you change scale and the path has gone: your hand searches, your head overloads. That’s cognitive chaos. So you go back to the scales you know, and the instrument that could play anything ends up playing only a small part of it.<
N013.note: « chaos cognitif » : gardé en cognitive chaos (mot fort de Yannick) plutôt que cognitive overload, terme courant mais redondant ici avec overloads. À trancher.

N014.en: >The chord in play: the hands show the movement.<

N015.en: >First month free. Connecting your Neotone stays free.<

N024.en: >A way of playing that works for major and minor scales.<

N025.en: >You have nothing to relearn when you change key.<

N026.en: >Like a capo on a guitar: whichever key you choose, your positions stay the same.<

N027.en: >You choose your key on the wheel, and Logic mode places it on your Neotone, major or minor. Your chords stay under the same fingers.<

N029.en: >Change key. The colours stay where they are.<

N030.en: >A chord keeps its shape and its colour: you recognise it at a glance, and your hand finds it again.<

N031.en: >An anchor note, so you never lose your way home<

N033.en: >The +7, +9, +11 enrichments laid out on the instrument<

N034.en: >Balance, Momentum, Adventure, Relaxation, Tension, Nostalgia, Mystery.<

N056.en: >Your Neotone and the app, synced in real time.<

N057.en: >You prepare your scales in the app and they go to your Neotone. And you can always see what’s loaded.<

N063.en: >The scale loaded on your Neotone, its concert pitch, the connection: you know where you stand before you play.<

N064.en: >Visual Quick Load: you grab a scale and drop it on a zone of your handpan. Click, drop. Set up one Quick Load for the concert and one for the lesson, and switch between them in one move.<

N065.en: >Your scales in the app and on your Neotone account, synced both ways. What’s missing on one side goes across from the other.<

N066.en: >Same notes, same octaves, same concert pitch: the app finds the copies. You choose which one to keep, and the others merge into it.<

N067.en: >What your Neotone has recorded: listen, download, sort into folders. And a MIDI file played by your Neotone.<
N067.note: « un fichier MIDI joué par ton Neotone » : fonction floue, traduit au plus près (le Neotone joue un fichier MIDI, ou fichier MIDI de ce qu’il a joué ?). Voir N113 « ton jeu enregistré, écrit en MIDI ».

N074.en: >Pick a region of the world, listen to a scale’s demo, and play it in your key.<

N075.en: >Discovering them is free. With Neotone Connection, in Studio, every scale you come across goes to your Neotone.<

N082.en: >Each with its own scales. And two instruments together play chords neither can play alone.<

N083.en: >In the same positions, a semitone or a third apart. Your duo memories, saved.<

N084.en: >The app writes to the Neotone the scale your acoustic is missing. It becomes its wild card.<

N085.en: >The app works out the placement, the fingering and the arpeggios.<

N092.en: >David Lesage was a beta tester for the Neotone, then its ambassador. He hit the same wall as you: notes that move with every scale. The app grew out of the drawings he made to find his way around.<

N121.en: >The Neotone¹ and the Neotone Mutant. And any MIDI instrument.<

N122.en: >Do I need Studio to connect my Neotone?<

N123.en: >No. Connecting it by USB or MIDI is free, with your playing shown in real time and the exercises for learning your scales. Studio opens up Neotone Connection, Logic mode and the duos.<

N125.en: >On a computer or tablet, in your browser. On a phone, the screen is too small to see your handpan and its chords properly. On iPhone and iPad, Apple stops browsers from receiving an instrument plugged in by USB: to connect a digital pan, open the app in Web MIDI Browser, free on the App Store.<

N127.en: >The app sees them together: that’s the hybrid duo, in Studio. And your acoustic gets everything that’s free in the app.<

N129.en: >We ask for your card when you sign up, but nothing is charged before the free month ends. After that, you stop whenever you like, from the following month.<

N136.en: Your Neotone can play every scale, and every change of scale creates cognitive chaos. Handpan Constellation Studio puts a visual memory on every scale: Logic mode, Neotone Connection and the Sound Atlas.
